recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中可見大型巨噬細胞，核小而偏位，細胞質豐富、淡藍灰色並有纖維狀條紋，呈「皺摺紙巾（wrinkled tissue paper）」外觀，與周圍紅血球和小型造血細胞相比大小懸殊，是典型的 Gaucher 細胞。
features: Very large macrophages, many times the diameter of adjacent red cells
Small, round to oval, eccentrically placed nucleus with coarse chromatin
Abundant pale blue-gray to pinkish cytoplasm with fibrillary striations (wrinkled tissue paper / crumpled silk appearance)
Occasional clustering of several Gaucher cells
Background erythroid precursors and red cells without prominent abnormality
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows several large macrophages with small eccentric nuclei and abundant pale blue-gray cytoplasm displaying a fibrillary, striated wrinkled tissue paper appearance. The cells occur singly and in small groups among erythroid precursors and red cells. Findings are consistent with Gaucher cells; in a child with massive splenomegaly and cytopenias this supports Gaucher disease, which must be confirmed by deficient beta-glucocerebrosidase activity or GBA1 genotyping.

ddx.dx: Pseudo-Gaucher cells (CML, myeloma, thalassemia, MAC infection)
ddx.vs: Pseudo-Gaucher cells look nearly identical but occur with an underlying neoplasm or infection and have normal glucocerebrosidase activity.
Niemann-Pick cells have foamy, finely vacuolated (bubbly) cytoplasm rather than fibrillary striations.
Sea-blue histiocytes contain coarse blue-green ceroid granules rather than a striated tissue-paper cytoplasm.
